renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: ccs_outcome_bars
  title: ZMW outcome per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library and each segment the outcome of its ZMWs: passed, or the filter that removed them, as a share of the ZMWs read. It answers where the ZMWs of each library went.
    How to read: a large Passed segment is a productive library. A large too-few-passes segment means short movies or long inserts, while a growing SNR or draft-failure segment points to the chemistry or the polymerase. Switch to counts to see the absolute numbers.
    Source: https://ccs.how/faq/fail-reads.html
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    default_rank: CCS outcome
    normalise_to_one: true
  roles:
    sample_id: library
    taxon: outcome
    rank: rank
    abundance: pct_of_input

- component: figure
  title: ZMW outcome share per library
  description: |-
    Each segment is an outcome of a library: its share of the ZMWs that went into CCS. It answers how the libraries compare on each filter.
    How to read: compare the same colour across libraries to see which one loses more ZMWs to a filter. The segments of a library add up to 100%.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: library
    y: pct_of_input
    color: outcome
    labels:
      library: Library
      pct_of_input: Share of input ZMWs (%)
      outcome: Outcome

- component: table
  title: CCS outcomes per library
  description: |-
    Each row is an outcome of one library: the number of ZMWs and their share of the ZMWs read. It answers exactly how many ZMWs each filter removed.
    How to read: sort by the share to see the dominant reason ZMWs fail.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: ccs_yield_plane
  title: ZMW depth against pass rate
  description: |-
    Each point is a library: the number of ZMWs read (horizontal) against the percentage that produced a CCS read (vertical), coloured by sample. It answers whether a library is short on depth, on pass rate, or on both.
    How to read: a library low on both lost its movie or was loaded poorly. A library low on the pass rate only lost its ZMWs to a filter, so open the outcome chart to see which one. ccs publishes no pass rate that separates good from bad libraries.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median CCS pass rate of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of pbccs.
    Source: https://ccs.how/
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: ZMWs read
    y_title: ZMWs giving a CCS read (%)
    legend_pos: bottom
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: zmw_input
    y: pct_passed
    label: library
    color: sample

- component: card
  title: ZMWs giving a CCS read
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of ZMWs that produced a CCS (HiFi) read, with the median and the largest library next to it. It answers how many reads the run yields.
    How to read: a large gap between the median and the maximum means uneven libraries. A HiFi read has a predicted accuracy of at least QV 20, and CCS reads below it go to the fail reads.
    Source: https://ccs.how/nomenclature.html and https://ccs.how/faq/fail-reads.html
  column: zmw_passed
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: per library, the median and the largest

- component: card
  title: CCS pass rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of ZMWs that gave a CCS read, with the spread across libraries in the box. It answers how efficient the consensus step is.
    How to read: a tight box is a consistent run. A library far below its peers lost ZMWs to a filter, so open the outcome chart to see which. ccs publishes no pass rate cut-off.
  column: pct_passed
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with the spread
  headline: true

- component: table
  title: CCS yield per library
  description: |-
    Each row is a library: the ZMWs read, passed and filtered, the pass rate and the main reasons for filtering. It answers how each library performed.
    How to read: sort by the pass rate to find libraries to check, then compare the filter columns.
